idiom_name: function type (Double) -> Double stored in the context, or a fun interface for named contracts
implementation_notes: Kotlin has function types as first-class citizens, so a strategy is a value of type (Double) -> Double: the context takes it as a constructor parameter or var, and the caller passes a lambda, a method reference (::price) or a partial application; typealias gives the contract a name without creating a type. The standard library follows the same route (sortedBy/sortedWith with a selector or Comparator, compareBy building comparators from lambdas), and SAM conversion turns a lambda into an implementation of any fun interface, so a declared single-method interface is interchangeable with the function type. Use a fun interface or a sealed interface with an exhaustive when when the strategies form a closed, nameable family or must be distinguished in logs and configuration.
pitfalls: Function types are structurally identical: two strategies with the same signature are interchangeable by accident and nothing in the type tells them apart, so name the contract with a typealias or a fun interface when the choice is configuration-driven.
Kotlin allows capturing mutable locals (unlike Java), which silently turns an intended stateless strategy into shared state when the lambda is stored and reused.

A when over strategies is exhaustive only while the subject is typed as the sealed hierarchy; declaring the parameter as the supertype interface removes the compiler's coverage check without a warning.
